'''Alex Ribeiro Garcia''', commonly known as either '''Alex Garcia''', or simply as '''Alex''' (born 4 March 1980) is a Brazilian professional [[basketball]] player. He also represented the senior [[Brazilian national basketball team|Brazilian national team]]. He is a {{convert|6|ft|3|in|m|adj=on}} {{convert|225|lb|kg}}<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/olympics/athletes/alex-garcia-1 Basketball-Reference.com Alex Garcia.]</ref> [[shooting guard]]-[[small forward]].

==Professional career==
Garcia has served two stints in the [[National Basketball Association]] as a member of the [[San Antonio Spurs]] ([[2003-04 NBA season|2003–04]]) and [[New Orleans Hornets]] ([[2004-05 NBA season|2004–05]]). He holds NBA career averages of 4.7 [[points per game]] and 1.8 [[assists per game]].<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/garcial01.html Basketball-Reference.com Alex Garcia.] Retrieved 27 August 2007.</ref> Garcia was promptly [[Waivers (sports)|waived]] by the hornets after suffering an [[anterior cruciate ligament injury]] vs. the [[Washington Wizards]] on December 12, 2004.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hornets Guard Alex Garcia Out For Season With Torn Anterior Cruciate|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/171612/Hornets-Guard-Alex-Garcia-Out-For-Season-With-Torn-Anterior-Cruciate|website=basketball.realgm.com|access-date=2020-05-12}}</ref>

This game with the ACL tear ended up being Garcia's final NBA game ever, as he spent the rest of his professional basketball career playing overseas. In that final game against the Wizards, Garcia recorded 6 points, 1 rebound and 2 steals as the Hornets lost the game 69 - 88.

Garcia has also played with [[UniCEUB/BRB]] and several other [[sports club|clubs]] of the top-tier level [[New Basket Brazil|Brazilian League]].

==National team career==
Garcia has been a member of the senior men's [[Brazilian national basketball team]].<ref>[http://cbs.sportsline.com/nba/story/10319131 James, Bryant, Anthony combine for 62 points as Americans roll easily.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070829133541/http://cbs.sportsline.com/nba/story/10319131 |date=August 29, 2007 }} CBSSports.com. 26 August 2007.</ref> With Brazil, he has played at the following major tournaments: the [[2002 FIBA World Cup]], the [[2003 FIBA AmeriCup]], the [[2005 FIBA AmeriCup]], the [[2006 FIBA World Cup]], the [[2007 FIBA AmeriCup]], the [[2009 FIBA AmeriCup]], the [[2010 FIBA World Cup]], the [[2011 FIBA AmeriCup]], the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]], the [[2013 FIBA AmeriCup]], the [[2014 FIBA World Cup]], and the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20181123154216/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/lid_38135_cp/1/pid/42361/q/Alex%20GARCIA/rpp//_//players.html Alex GARCIA (BRA).]</ref>
